PHYSICS — TERMLY EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mechanical Properties of Materials? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mechanical Properties of Materials.

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pressure? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pressure.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Pressure.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pressure.

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Moments and equilibrium? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Moments and equilibrium.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Moments and equilibrium.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Moments and equilibrium.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Moments and equilibrium.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Physics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Physics.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Physics.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Physics.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.

13. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Waves? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Waves.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Waves.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Waves.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Waves.

15. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Electronics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change 4.2 Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 o and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 of 62 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL P and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Space Physics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Physics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
